lesson.title: Friction Force Lab: Static vs. Kinetic
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 3 Lesson 3: Friction Force Lab - Static vs. Kinetic

gradingDesign.rule: Only lessons with a completed provided chart use 10 automatic points; variable student evidence is graded in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: Record Wood's peak static force from the Part 1 graph. ________ N
Record Rubber's sliding kinetic force from the Part 1 graph. ________ N
Calculate Sandpaper's coefficient of static friction from the completed chart. ________
For Wood with 5 kg added, what normal force belongs in the Part 2 chart? ________ N
For Wood with 10 kg added, record the peak static force. ________ N
What coefficient of static friction should all three Wood added-mass rows show, within rounding? ________
Unknown A has a mass of 5.0 kg. What normal force should be used for its coefficient calculations? ________ N
Use Unknown A's 27.0 N static peak and 49.1 N normal force to calculate mu_s. ________
Which coefficient pair matches Unknown A?
Which statement matches the force-time graphs in this lab?
Use at least three values from your completed charts to explain how material and added mass affect maximum static friction, kinetic friction, mu_s, and mu_k.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: The analysis should distinguish force changes from coefficient changes and cite the student's chart.
a. Full credit: Uses at least three accurate chart values, explains that material determines the coefficients, and explains that added mass increases normal and friction forces while Wood's coefficients remain about 0.42 and 0.25.
  Partial credit: Gives the correct relationships but includes limited chart evidence or omits one coefficient.
  No credit: Gives no chart evidence or claims the coefficients increase with added mass.

questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion for all three parts. Distinguish static from kinetic friction, identify Unknown A by its coefficients, and explain the added-mass result. Include one realistic source of uncertainty and one improvement.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Synthesize the lab with chart and graph evidence rather than listing definitions.
a. Full credit: Makes a correct claim, cites several values including Unknown A near 0.55 and 0.35, explains the added-mass result, distinguishes static and kinetic friction, and gives a plausible graph-reading or rounding uncertainty with a specific improvement.
  Partial credit: Gives a mostly correct conclusion but omits one required evidence or evaluation element.
  No credit: Provides an unsupported conclusion or confuses the main friction relationships.
